mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks (rising from -28.6% to -19.6%) signals normalization of commuting patterns. This recovery will compound over the next four weeks, driving weekday retail footfall and lifting RETAIL_REC above its recent baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative PARKS mobility (declining from -9.4% to -18.0%) indicates suppressed outdoor leisure activity. As weather patterns shift or behavioral adaptation occurs, PARKS recovery will redirect foot traffic from residential confinement to retail-and-recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 8.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -15% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -45% over the past three weeks, indicating a floor in commuting suppression. When TRANSIT rises above -40%, it signals confidence in public transport use and enables retail cluster access, triggering a multiplicative effect on RETAIL_REC through increased foot traffic density.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40% in any week
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -45% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT breach above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable and elevated (7.3–7.4%) over four weeks, indicating sustained essential-goods demand. This stability, combined with the approach of the Australian summer holiday season (late November onwards), will trigger discretionary retail spending as consumers shift from essential to recreational shopping, raising RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained between 6.3% and 7.4% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% in any week ahead.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily (from 9.6% to 6.9%), indicating reduced home confinement. This trend signals increased willingness to leave home for non-essential activities. If RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% in the next week, it will trigger a compensatory surge in RETAIL_REC as pent-up demand for out-of-home recreation is released.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not fall below 6% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 6%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of stable GROCERY_PHARM (indicating maintained essential-goods access) and improving WORKPLACES (rising 9 points over four weeks) signals that mobility restrictions are easing. Under a reopening regime, this dual signal will unlock retail-and-recreation spending as confidence in public health improves, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20% AND GROCERY_PHARM remains above 6%
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES falls below -25% or GROCERY_PHARM drops below 5% in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 28-day mean.

If TRANSIT remains below -45% for the next two weeks, it signals continued transport constraints that will suppress retail access and keep RETAIL_REC depressed below its recent mean.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not risen above -45.6% in the past four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -40% in any week ahead, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT remaining suppressed below -45%.
